items.title: Toward an automated science of the mind
items.author: Akshay K. Jagadish, Milena Rmus, Kristin Witte, Marvin Mathony, Marcel Binz, Eric Schulz
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence is starting to automate scientific discovery, raising the prospect of an automated science of the mind. We chart this field around four challenges: representing experiments, generating synthetic behavior, synthesizing models, and closing the loop to discover psychological theories.</article>

items.title: How private foundations and governments helped build theoretical neuroscience
items.author: Xiao-Jing Wang
items.content: <article>Visionary philanthropy and governments worked with scientists to develop theoretical and computational neuroscience, through establishing centers with “local critical mass,” training “outsiders,” and fostering theory-experiment collaborations. This NeuroView traces how those bets shaped the field, helping launch AI and computational psychiatry.</article>

items.title: Neuroscience and AI: Emerging synergies
items.author: Christina Konen, Mariela Zirlinger
items.content: <article>This issue marks the second installment in a three-part series that Neuron is devoting to NeuroAI this year. The series reflects a field that is moving unusually fast in both directions: artificial systems are increasingly used as working models of the brain, and the brain is increasingly invoked to explain why artificial systems work at all. That exchange, no longer a curiosity at the margins of either discipline, has become an engine driving progress in both.</article>

items.title: The recipe for intelligence in natural and artificial systems
items.author: Christopher Summerfield, Kimberly Stachenfeld
items.content: <article>This review by Summerfield and Stachenfeld surveys how the dialog between neuroscience and AI research has evolved over the past decade. They highlight continued opportunities for synergy between these disciplines.</article>
